messages:
Priya: Hey team — customer AcmeCorp reporting a sudden p99 spike to ~12s for text-gen during their nightly invoice batch (around 02:00 UTC). They also saw a handful of 502s and some 401s during the window. Raising an incident for triage.

Alex: Thanks Priya. Do we have a request ID or trace to follow?

Priya: request_id=rcx-20260317-9f4a, sample logs attached by customer (trimmed). They say it started right at the billing cutover.

Maria: Noted. I'll pull infra metrics for that window. Can someone confirm if their traffic was routed to a Dedicated pool or Hosted?

Priya: They are on Dedicated (reserved pool: acmecorp-prod-6).

Sunil: I'm seeing a sharp rise in concurrent attaches to that pool at 02:00. Provisioning queue spiked and several pods reported long warmup times. p99 token latency lines up with attach/warmup latency in the same timeslice.

Jason: Any evidence of cold GPU starts or image pulls causing delay?

Sunil: Yes — kernel image pull times spiked on 3 nodes and GPU attach timeouts increased. Some nodes also logged OOM while initializing the model cache.

Nate: Customer also reported auth 401s — could be token refresh/rotation during billing job. I see auth service rps to our token-exchange endpoint spike at same time and ~0.2% 5xx.

Priya: They ran a high-concurrency job that bursts for ~90s each invoice batch. Default autoscale policy didn't prewarm enough.

Alex: Repro hypothesis: heavy burst -> attach fanout -> provisioning queue -> image pulls + model cache init -> p99 spike & occasional 502s. 401s from auth timeouts.

Maria: Short-term mitigation options: 1) increase minpool for acmecorp-prod-6 (hotfix), 2) enable prewarm for their schedule (cron-based), 3) temporary routing to a standby pool in another AZ. Which do we prefer?

Jason: I'd push minpool up to handle their known billing burst pattern. Also enable proactive prewarm (we have scripts to schedule warmup cron). Manual routing is riskier during billing window.

Sunil: If we increase minpool, we should also bump model cache size reservation to avoid OOM on init. I'll prepare a config change.

Nate: For the 401s, ask customer to retry with exponential backoff and ensure token refresh isn't coordinated across workers. We can also slow-roll their job to spread attach over 2 mins.

Priya: Action items: @Sunil apply minpool + cache reservation for acmecorp-prod-6; @Alex coordinate prewarm cron; @Nate send repro guidance to customer and get their job sample; @Maria monitor after changes. I'll alert customer with ETA 30m.

Sunil: Starting change now. Patch: set min_pool_replicas=12 -> 24, model_cache_mb=40960 -> 61440. Applying to pool acmecorp-prod-6.

deploy-bot: deploy start: pool-config-update acmecorp-prod-6 by Sunil at 2026-03-17T02:45:10Z

ops-bot: rolling update progress: node-3 failed image-pull, retrying.

Sunil: Image-pull retry fixed by increasing registry concurrency backoff. All nodes now show ready and prewarm tasks running.

Maria: Metrics post-change: attach queue depth reduced from 28 -> 4, p99 generation latency dropped from ~12s -> 1.8s within 6 minutes. No 502s after warmup finished.

Nate: Customer ran a test batch with staggered start; auth 401s disappeared after we added jitter advice.

Priya: Customer confirms throughput returned to normal during next invoice batch. They've accepted recommended permanent fixes: scheduled prewarm and increased minpool for billing windows.

Alex: Follow-ups: add a detection rule for billing-window spikes (pattern: scheduled high-concurrency from same account at fixed UTC time) to auto-suggest prewarm. Also log correlation between auth spike and attach surge.

Maria: I'll draft a short runbook for support: - how to check pool attach queue, - quick minpool hotfix command, - model cache tweak, - auth retry guidance.

Priya: Great. Closing this thread once the runbook is in GH and customer confirmed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
